title: Packers hold on to beat Bears, 28-21
text_body: Packers hold on to beat Bears, 28-21 Keisean Nixon’s late INT moves Green Bay into first place Dec 07, 2025 at 05:00 PM by Wes Hodkiewicz & Mike Spofford Copied! Todd Rosenberg/NFL QB Jordan Love and WR Christian Watson GREEN BAY – Packers CB Keisean Nixon intercepted Bears QB Caleb Williams' fourth-and-1 pass into the end zone with 22 seconds left to give Green Bay a 28-21 victory over Chicago on Sunday at Lambeau Field. With the win, the Packers improved to 9-3-1 and moved into first place in the NFC North, just ahead of the 9-4 Bears. The two teams meet again in two weeks at Soldier Field. Chicago trailed 14-3 at halftime and 21-11 in the second half but rallied to tie the game at 21 midway through the fourth quarter. The Bears pounded away with their ground game, and Green Bay's offense went three-and-out twice in the second half. After the game was tied, the Packers responded with a 65-yard TD drive, capped by a Josh Jacobs run, to retake the lead. The Bears countered on their final drive with two pass completions of 20-plus yards and eventually got into the red zone. But the Packers stopped a third-and-1 run from the 14, and then on fourth-and-1, Williams rolled left off a play fake and tried to loft a pass for TE Cole Kmet in the end zone. But Nixon was in front of him and leaped for the interception to seal the win. For the Packers, QB Jordan Love was 17-of-25 for 234 yards with three TDs, one INT, and a 120.7 passer rating. WR Christian Watson caught four passes for 89 yards and two TDs, and WR Bo Melton caught a 45-yard TD, his only reception of the game. WR Jayden Reed , back from injury, caught four passes for 31 yards and ran twice for 22 more. Jacobs finished with 20 carries for 86 yards and a TD. For the Bears, Williams was 19-of-35 for 186 yards with two TDs and one INT for a 76.6 rating. WR Luther Burden III had four catches for 67 yards, Kmet had two catches for 42, and TE Colston Loveland had four catches for 29 yards and a score. WR Olamide Zaccheaus had the other TD reception for Chicago. RB D'Andre Swift had 13 carries for 63 yards, and RB Kyle Monongai had 14 carries for 57 yards. Here's a recap of all the action: Todd Rosenberg/NFL Packers and Bears play a scoreless first quarter Green Bay won the toss and deferred. The Bears went three-and-out on their first possession after Caleb Williams missed two receivers high on second and third down. Xavier McKinney nearly sacked Williams on second-and-5, but right tackle Darnell Wright was still called for a hold. Green Bay started at its 11 after a Tory Taylor punt and block in the back. In his first game since Week 2, Jayden Reed touched the ball three times on the Packers' first seven plays. He converted a third-and-1 with a 2-yard play action pass. Josh Jacobs picked up three yards on third-and-3 from the Chicago 46. Emanuel Wilson gained another six before the Packers went hurry-up and Montez Sweat sacked Jordan Love for a 14-yard loss. C.J. Gardner-Johnson picked off Love on the next play and returned the ball to the Packers' 36. On first down, it was initially ruled a completed pass to tight end Colston Loveland, but Head Coach Matt LaFleur challenged after safety Evan Williams punched the ball out. It was overturned to an incompletion upon review. Chicago didn't get any points off the takeaway after a false start penalty and Micah Parsons forcing a scrambling Williams to throw the ball away on third-and-15. The Packers once again took over at their 11. Green Bay opened the drive with a 5-yard Jacobs run and a 19-yard slant to Christian Watson to the Green Bay 35. On the next play, Love aired out a deep ball to tight end Luke Musgrave that was overturned upon a Chicago challenge. A facemask penalty on Aaron Banks backed Green Bay up 15 yards. Green Bay gained six yards on a quick pass to Reed but was forced to punt after Love's third-and-19 pass for Romeo Doubs sailed high. The Bears took over at their 25 after a 55-yard Daniel Whelan punt and 6-yard return. D'Andre Swift picked up the initial first down after gaining 12 yards on back-to-back carries, but that's all the Bears would get. Parsons pressured Williams into another throwaway on third-and-7. The Packers took over at their 20 after a touchback. The first quarter ended on a 7-yard Jacobs run. Morry Gash/AP Packers lead Bears 14-3 at halftime John FitzPatrick powered through Gardner-Johnson for eight yards on first-and-10 from the Green Bay 32. After Jacobs broke through for seven yards on third-and-1, FitzPatrick caught a 6-yard pass to move the Packers past midfield. On third-and-2, Darian Kinnard reported eligible as a sixth offensive lineman and the Packers ran a play-action pass for Josh Whyle that gained 21 yards to the Chicago 23. Green Bay converted its fifth third down with a 23-yard touchdown pass from Love to Christian Watson to put the Packers up 7-0 with nine minutes, 19 seconds left in the half. Williams rolled right on third-and-3 and connected with Luther Burden to push the ball to the Chicago 45. An illegal hands to face penalty aided the Bears on their next first down to move the ball across midfield. Williams ran a 5-yard bootleg on fourth-and-1 after three Kyle Monangai runs gained nine yards. Monangai gained just a yard on first down at the 34, but the Bears moved into the red zone because of an unnecessary roughness penalty. Defensive lineman Karl Brooks tackled D.J. Moore for a 4-yard loss on the next play. A 6-yard Monangai run brought the clock down to the two-minute warning. Chicago settled for a 33-yard Cairo Santos field goal to cut Green Bay's lead to 7-3 with 1:14 left in the first half. The Packers started at their own 40 after Santos' kickoff fell short of the landing zone. The Packers used their first timeout after a 12-yard pass to Musgrave. With plenty of time to throw, Love aired out a 45-yard touchdown pass to Bo Melton to put the Packers up 14-3 with 38 seconds left in the second quarter. It was the longest catch of Melton's career and his first touchdown since 2023. Chicago gained 12 yards on a pass to Loveland but lost nine after Kingsley Enagbare sacked Williams on the next play. The Bears used their first timeout with 21 seconds left in the half. Green Bay called timeout after Swift picked up nine yards on third-and-18. Todd Rosenberg/NFL Packers lead Bears 21-14 after three quarters Green Bay went three-and-out to start the second half after Love threw the ball away on first down, Jacobs lost a yard on second down and Melton was flagged for offensive pass interference on third down. Chicago took over at its 36 after Whelan's 40-yard punt bounced out of bounds. The Bears gained the initial first down on a 6-yard pass to Olamide Zaccheaus and a 6-yard Williams scramble. Loveland caught a 10-yard pass to the Green Bay 37 on third-and-5. A 26-yard pass to Cole Kmet set up first-and-10 at the Packers' 11. The Bears scored on a 1-yard touchdown pass to Zaccheaus to cut Green Bay's lead to 14-11 with 8:20 left in the third quarter after Monangai's successful two-point conversion. The Packers started at their 37 after Melton's 30-yard kickoff return. Reed gained 15 yards on an end-around to start the drive. On third-and-3, Watson caught a quick slant from Love and outran Gardner-Johnson to the end zone for a 41-yard touchdown to extend Green Bay's lead to 21-11 with 6:10 left in the third quarter. Chicago started at its 40 after Brandon McManus ' kickoff went out of bounds. Williams opened with a 16-yard pass to Kmet on a rollout and then hit Burden for 18 yards to the Green Bay 26. The Chicago drive stalled after a Burden reverse gained just three yards and Green Bay blew up a receiver screen. Santos made a 41-yard field goal to cut the Packers' lead to 21-14 with 3:15 left in the third quarter. The Packers went three-and-out after a deep ball for Doubs fell incomplete and Love settled for a 6-yard checkdown to Chris Brooks on third-and-10. Chicago started at its 17 after Whelan's 50-yard punt wasn't returned. Monangai gained nine yards on third-and-1 to end the third quarter. Todd Rosenberg/NFL Packers hold off Bears 28-21, move into first place in NFC North Swift converted a third-and-1 with a 7-yard run up the middle to the Green Bay 49. An elaborate shovel pass to Swift gained eight yards on second-and-3 for a first down. Craig Wrolstad's crew incorrectly gave Williams a first down on a scramble, which LaFleur challenged to push the ball back to the 25. On third-and-1, Swift gained eight up the middle. Chicago converted another third down with a 10-yard flare to Burden on third-and-8, setting up first-and-goal at the Green Bay 5. On third-and-goal, Williams found an open Loveland to tie the game at 21 with eight minutes left in regulation. The 17-play scoring drive lasted 8:32. Green Bay took over at its 35 after a touchback. Jacobs gained 11 yards on first down, setting up an 18-yard play-action pass to Reed to the Chicago 36. Green Bay used its first timeout with 5:20 left after a 6-yard pass to Jacobs in the flat on second-and-8. On the next play, Jacobs cut back on a pitch and made two Bears miss on a 21-yard gain to the Chicago 7. Bears cornerback Nahshon Wright was injured at the end of Emanuel Wilson's 3-yard stretch left on first-and-goal. Green Bay moved to the Chicago 2 after neutral zone infraction on second down. Jacobs powered in the end zone on a third-and-2 draw to put the Packers back up 28-21 with 3:32 remaining. Chicago started at its 26 after Arron Mosby stopped Devin Duvernay. On first down, Williams found an open Burden for 27 yards to the Packers' 47. He then hit Duvernay for 24 yards as the game reached the two-minute warning. Two Monangai carries set up third-and-1 at the Green Bay 14 as the clock ticked under one minute. Enagbare stopped Monangai for no gain on third-and-1. The Bears used their first timeout with 27 seconds remaining. On fourth down, Keisean Nixon picked off Williams in the end zone on a pass intended for Kmet to seal it.

text_body: Postgame Recap Presented by Bears 31, Browns 3 | Final Score, Stats & Game Recap Myles Garrett records 1.5 sacks in loss to Chicago Dec 14, 2025 at 04:39 PM Noah Monroe Staff Writer Intern Copied! The Browns struggled to generate offensive pressure against a stout Bears' defense, scoring three points and turning the ball over three times. Cleveland fell to Chicago 31-3 on Dec. 14 at Soldier Field as the Browns dropped their 11 th game this season. QB Shedeur Sanders threw for 177 yards, including 42- and 47-yard passes to WR Isaiah Bond . TE Harold Fannin Jr. added 48 yards on seven catches while WR Jerry Jeudy caught two passes for 22 yards. Sanders led the Browns with 24 rushing yards while RB Quinshon Judkins gained 21 rushing yards on 11 carries. The Browns' defense allowed 31 points for the second consecutive week, including 14 each in the first and third quarter. LB Carson Schwesinger led the defense in tackles with 14 total tackles, while LB Mohamoud Diabate had eight total tackles and S Ronnie Hickman added seven total tackles. DE Myles Garrett tallied 1.5 sacks and DE Alex Wright picked up a sack, bringing him to four this season. DT Shelby Harris added half a sack. Key Moments Myles Garrett records 1.5 sacks to bring his season total to 21.5 sacks With the Bears at the Browns' 8-yard line on third-and-goal, Garrett sprinted past Bears OL Ozzy Trapilo and sacked QB Caleb Williams as he tried to escape through the pocket. Garrett ended Chicago's chances of taking a 21-0 lead with his 21 st sack of the season. Bears K Cairo Santos missed the 35-yard field goal on fourth down, clanging the ball off the right upright and keeping the Bears' lead at 14-0. Garrett notched a half sack and his 21.5 this season in the fourth quarter, combining with Harris for the sack. On third-and-15, Garrett ran past Trapilo again and met Harris as the pair sandwiched and sacked Williams to the ground for a loss of eight yards. The sack moved the Bears from the Cleveland 46-yard line to their own 46-yard line and forced their fourth punt of the game. The game was Garrett's sixth multi-sack game this season and puts him a sack away from tying the NFL single-season sack record of 22.5 with three games remaining in the season. He added four total tackles and three quarterback hits in the loss. Bears turn Browns' interceptions into points The Browns received the ball back with 8:53 left in the third quarter and a chance to narrow the Bears' lead to one possession, but it was cut short by Chicago's defense. Sanders threw a pass over the middle but Bears LB D'Marco Jackson tipped the ball into the air and made the interception. Jackson was taken down at the Cleveland 22-yard line. A play later, Williams rolled out to the right and fired a pass past two Browns defenders to WR DJ Moore for a touchdown, giving the Bears a 21-3 lead in the third quarter. On Cleveland's next offensive possession, Sanders threw his second interception. CB Jaylon Johnson picked off a pass that fell through Jeudy's arms in the end zone, setting the Bears up at their own 20-yard line. Chicago moved down the field with a nine-play, 75-yard touchdown drive that was finished by a 17-yard touchdown run by RB D'Andre Swift. With 9:10 remaining in the fourth quarter, Sanders tried to loft a pass to Fannin but Bears S C.J. Gardner-Johnson leapt up to make the interception. He returned the turnover for a gain of 32 yards to the Cleveland 22-yard line. The Browns' defense forced Chicago to lose a yard combined on the next three plays and Santos made a 41-yard field goal to give Chicago a 31-3 lead. Bears score on back-to-back possessions in the first quarter The Bears' offense was stopped for a three-and-out on their first possession of the game but found the end zone on their second and third possessions to take an early lead. Swift ran for 21 yards on four carries, including a 10-yard run to put Chicago in the red zone on the Bears' first scoring drive of the afternoon. He recorded his first rushing touchdown of the game with a 6-yard run to put the Bears up 7-0 with 7:35 left in the first quarter. The Bears' second scoring drive of the game was aided by two consecutive long gains on pass plays by Williams. TE Colston Loveland gained 24 yards and moved the Bears past midfield to the Cleveland 48-yard line. Williams and WR Luther Burden connected for 40 yards, putting the Bears in the red zone. Three plays later, Williams found Moore in the back of the end zone and giving the Bears a 14-0 lead. Game Highlights Shedeur Sanders fires a deep pass to Isaiah Bond for a 42-yard gain. Andre Szmyt makes a 50-yard field goal to put the Browns on the board. Shedeur Sanders fights off a sack and connects with Harold Fannin Jr. for a first down. Shedeur Sanders finds Isaiah Bond down the field again, this time for a 47-yard gain. title: Instant analysis of Bears' 31-3 win vs. Browns in Week 15
text_body: BEARS Instant analysis of Bears' 31-3 win vs. Browns in Week 15 Vincent Parise Bears Wire Dec. 14, 2025, 5:11 p.m. CT The Chicago Bears defeated the Cleveland Browns with a final score of 31-3. Chicago's defense forced three interceptions, bringing their league-leading takeaway total to 30. Running back D'Andre Swift scored two touchdowns, while quarterback Caleb Williams threw for two more. The victory marks the Bears' 10th win of the season under first-year head coach Ben Johnson. The Chicago Bears blew out the Cleveland Browns, 31-3, Sunday at Soldier Field. It was a chilly affair, making it one of the more difficult games of the season right off the bat. Early in the game, special teams were on top of their game. Devin Duvernay returned the opening kickoff to midfield, and the punt unit pinned the Browns offense on the one-yard line after the Bears couldn’t score on their opening possession. After making a defensive stop when Cleveland was pinned in, Chicago took a 7-0 lead. Running back D’Andre Swift scored his sixth touchdown of the season, and Cairo Santos hit the extra point. From there, the Bears were off and running. Eventually, they took a 14-0 lead, and only climbed up from there. The final score of 31-3 tells the story perfectly of how much the Bears dominated the football game. Chicago is now 10-4 in head coach Ben Johnson's first year. A double-digit win season was not a lock for the Bears coming into 2025, especially after starting the year 0-2. Everyone from the coaching staff to the executives to the players should be proud of the year that they are putting together. Quarterback Caleb Williams completed 17-of-28 passes for 242 yards with two touchdown passes and no interceptions. It wasn't a perfect outing for him out in the cold, but he made some big-time throws when he needed to. Williams and the offense accounted for four touchdowns, so it was more than good enough. In the run game, Swift carried the load with 18 carries for 98 yards, averaging 5.4 yards per carry, and two touchdowns. Kyle Monangai, who has had a great rookie year, carried it for 33 yards on 11 carries. It is hard to say which of these guys is going to be the biggest difference maker from week to week, but one of them always seems to step up. The Chicago Bears defeated the Cleveland Browns in blowout fashion, 31-3, on Sunday to improve to 10-4 on the season. The Bears absolutely blew the doors off the Browns, and it was exactly the kind of win you wanted to see. Chicago beat up on a bad team ahead of a pivotal divisional showdown against the Green Bay Packers next week. The Bears offense put up 31 points, including two-touchdown days from wide receiver DJ Moore and running back D'Andre Swift. Meanwhile, the defense allowed just three points and totaled five sacks while forcing three more turnovers (all interceptions of Shedeur Sanders) in an overall dominant outing. There were plenty of standout players in Chicago's most decisive win this season. With that in mind, here's a look at the biggest studs from the Bears' blowout win vs. Browns: QB Caleb Williams Quarterback Caleb Williams has been criticized for his completion percentage this season, but there's no denying his ability to create magic on the field. Williams did just that in this blowout win, which included an insane throw on a 22-yard passing touchdown to receiver DJ Moore. Williams completed 17-of-28 passes for 242 yards with two touchdowns and zero interceptions and a 112.5 passer rating. LB D'Marco Jackson There have been several success stories for the Bears this season, including linebacker D'Marco Jackson, who has come up big for Chicago with injuries at linebacker to T.J. Edwards (now back in the lineup) and Tremaine Edmunds (on IR). Jackson had a monster game against the Browns, where he totaled seven tackles, including one tackle for loss, one sack, one QB hit, one interception and two pass breakups. He received a game ball from Ben Johnson after the game. WR DJ Moore After Rome Odunze reaggravated his foot injury during warmups, the Bears needed a receiver to step up. They had a couple (more on Luther Burden III late), but veteran DJ Moore picked the perfect time for one of his better games of the season. Moore had four catches for 69 yards on five targets with two touchdowns, including one on an insane throw from Caleb Williams. RB D'Andre Swift Running back D'Andre Swift led the Bears' top-two rushing attack, which totaled 142 yards on the day, with 18 carries for 98 yards, averaging 5.4 yards per carry, and two touchdowns. That included an impressive 17-yard rushing score that put Chicago up 28-3. Swift continues to find success in this Ben Johnson offense, and he was key on the ground to help open things up in the pass game. Booker totaled two sacks, four QB hits and four tackles on Sunday. And he nearly had a strip-sack and subsequent fumble recovery if the refs didn't controversially rule forward progress on Shedeur Sanders on a third-down stop. author: Brendan Sugrue
title: 6 Takeaways from the Bears' dominant win vs. Browns
text_body: BEARS 6 Takeaways from the Bears' dominant win vs. Browns Brendan Sugrue Bears Wire Updated Dec. 16, 2025, 8:37 a.m. CT The Chicago Bears defeated the Cleveland Browns 31-3, improving their season record to 10-4. Quarterback Caleb Williams threw for two touchdowns, while running back D'Andre Swift rushed for two more. Chicago's defense held the Browns to a single field goal, forcing three turnovers and five sacks. Despite the win, Head Coach Ben Johnson's handling of the final seconds of the first half drew some criticism. A Chicago Bears victory Monday never felt more relaxing. The Bears took care of business over the weekend when they disposed of the Cleveland Browns, winning 31-3 on the lakefront and improving to 10-4 on the season. Despite the frigid temperatures at Soldier Field, the Bears started out hot with a quick 14-0 lead in the first half and rarely let up. Quarterback Caleb Williams led the offense on five scoring drives while delivering two touchdown passes on the day. Running back D'Andre Swift ran hard for two scores of his own, and the Bears easily controlled the clock on offense with sustained drives. Defensively, Chicago had Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders in a blender. The rookie was forced into three turnovers and was sacked five times by the Bears' front. The Browns could only muster a field goal and continued their touchdown drought at Soldier Field, which goes back to 2009. The Bears needed to take care of business against a lowly Browns team to continue their trek towards the postseason, and they accomplished that mission. Before we turn the page to the Green Bay Packers, here are our takeaways from Sunday's game: 1. Caleb Williams owns Soldier Field Williams has produced a handful of standout games at Soldier Field this season, and this one may have been his best. The second-year quarterback was locked in all day, completing 17 of 28 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns. He arguably had his best throw of the year on his second score when he found DJ Moore streaking across the back of the end zone and made a cross-body throw that most passers wouldn't dream of trying. It wasn't just the flash plays, though. Williams was dialed in with accurate passes, both short and long, with poise. He just seems to have a different feel to him at home vs. on the road—even in the bitter cold. In six games at Soldier Field, Williams has thrown 11 touchdowns and just one interception while completing 59% of his passes for a passer rating of 91.4. In eight games on the road, he has 10 touchdowns to five interceptions while completing 57% of his passes for a passer rating of 82.6. Williams isn't bad on the road, but he operates at a different level at home. If the Bears can secure the NFC North and make teams come to Soldier Field, that would bode extremely well for Williams. If the Bears somehow land the No. 1 seed in the conference, then I expect Williams to be hoisting the George Halas Trophy. 2. D'Andre Swift is playing exceptional football We don't need to do the Swift apology tour again. That's been over and done with for a while now. But Swift has turned a good season into a great one over the last few weeks, and he exemplified that with his performance on Sunday. Swift ran for 98 yards on 18 carries, just two yards shy of his fourth 100-yard rushing game of the season. He ran with a unique mix of violence and precision against a formidable Browns run defense as he bounced off multiple tacklers for big gains. Swift is easily having the best season of his career with 935 rushing yards on 191 carries through 13 games. For context, he totaled 959 yards last season with 62 more attempts. And he already has converted 54 first downs, 11 more than last year's season total. While Kyle Monangai has been an excellent complement to Swift, this is still his backfield. He's playing exceptional football and should be a staple going into next season instead of a cut candidate. 3. Ben Johnson mishandled the end of the first half So many things went right during Sunday's game that nitpicking the imperfections feels unfair, but Ben Johnson cannot be left off the hook for a poor showing going into halftime. The Bears got the ball with 40 seconds left and all three timeouts following a Browns three-and-out at their own 26-yard line. Williams quickly delivered a strike to Moore that put the offense at midfield with 33 seconds left and called a timeout. A pair of dropped passes stalled the drive, but the Bears were able to gain seven yards on third and three to give themselves a shot with 23 seconds left and two timeouts. Johnson opted to let the clock run down, call a timeout, and attempt a hook and ladder play as time expired to try and get into the end zone. It was never close. I understand not wanting the Browns to have a chance to possess the ball, but the Bears were up by two scores with a chance to make it a three-score game. Johnson should have been more aggressive with getting points in that situation. Thankfully, it didn't matter in the end, but it's the principle of the matter. The Bears haven't executed the end-of-half sequence well in recent weeks, and I'd like to see that get cleaned up. 4. DJ Moore shut me up A week ago, I wrote how Moore simply doesn't fit the Bears' offense and there isn't a place for him following his one-catch, negative-yardage game against the Packers. That may have been an overreaction. Moore may not be the weekly dependable WR1 like we saw a couple of years ago, but he and Williams have an underrated chemistry. That insane cross-body throw isn't going to just any pass catcher after all. Moore, like Williams, is a scoring threat when playing at Soldier Field. All five of his touchdowns this season have come at home, and Williams loves to look his way inside the red zone. Moore made smooth catches down the middle of the field and near the sideline. With Rome Odunze likely out for at least a couple of weeks and Luther Burden's status in the air, Moore will be relied upon even more. And games like Sunday will help set the tone for the rest of the season. 5. Bears defense got the biggest impact from unlikely players It's been a while since the Bears defense could have their way with an inexperienced offense, and they took advantage against Sanders and the Browns. The rookie looked lost facing Dennis Allen's unit for much of the day, but it wasn't the usual suspects like Montez Sweat or TJ Edwards making the big plays. Defensive end Austin Booker and linebacker D'Marco Jackson were the stars of the day. Jackson finished second on the team with seven total tackles with one for loss but made the tide-turning interception early in the third quarter. Jackson immediately recognized where the ball was going after initially pursuing Sanders and tipped a pass to himself for the pick. Ever since he was thrust into action with all of the injuries to the linebackers, he hasn't allowed the defense to miss a beat. Booker, meanwhile, has arguably his best game as a pro. The 2024 fifth-round pick totaled four tackles, two for loss, two sacks, six pressures, and four QB hits. He was giving the Browns tackles fits all day long, and it forced Sanders into bad throws and costly mistakes. It's great to see players who were once just role players capitalize with massive plays deep into the season with playoff implications at stake. The Bears are going to continue to need that type of play. 6. This is a good football team Good football teams beat up on bad football teams. And they do it with a bigger prize in mind. That's exactly what this Bears team did. Players were happy with the win, yet talked about the bitter taste in their mouths from the Packers loss a week earlier. Johnson has done a fine job of keeping the focus on the next game while also making sure his players know there is more out there. And now it's time to shift the focus back to Green Bay and hang onto the division lead. Sciatica Is Not from a Slipped Disc. title: Instant analysis from Bears' improbable comeback win vs. Packers
text_body: BEARS Instant analysis from Bears' improbable comeback win vs. Packers Vincent Parise Bears Wire Dec. 20, 2025 Updated Dec. 21, 2025, 12:28 a.m. CT The Chicago Bears defeated the Green Bay Packers 22-16 in an overtime victory on Saturday night. Quarterback Caleb Williams threw a walk-off touchdown pass to receiver DJ Moore in overtime to secure the win. The Bears' offense struggled early, scoring zero points in the first half before mounting a fourth-quarter comeback. Green Bay's starting quarterback, Jordan Love, left the game with a concussion and was replaced by backup Malik Willis. With the win, the Bears remain in first place in the NFC North and hold the second seed in the NFC. The Chicago Bears defeated the Green Bay Packers, 22-16, in overtime on Saturday night. They were losing for most of the game, but they once again mounted some late-game heroics to find a way to pull out the improbable win. They recovered an onside kick, scored when it mattered most, and made the necessary plays in OT to get it done. The Bears did not have a perfect game. They are dealing with some injuries, but they found a way to win a football game that was incredibly difficult against their arch-rival. The offense was stag in the first half. They scored zero points in the first 30 minutes and were trailing 6-0 at halftime. The defense was playing its brand of "bend-don't-break," and it was enough. But the offense wasn't living up to its end of the bargain. In the second half, things didn't get off to a strong start during a miserable third quarter that totaled just three points for Chicago. But the fourth quarter was once again the turning point as the Bears rattled off three straight scoring drives, including two field goals and the game-tying touchdown from quarterback Caleb Williams to rookie receiver Jahdae Walker to force overtime. In overtime, once the Packers turned the ball over on downs, the Bears just needed one big play. After some short yard gains, Williams made a big throw to receiver DJ Moore down the field, which ended in the walk-off score. The Bears were in danger of being swept by the Packers. That would have put their playoff hopes in jeopardy, but they found a way to get it done. Losing would have proved that they are not worthy of being a playoff team with the elites in the NFC. Instead, they remain in first of the NFC North, which is a great division, and they will stick in the second seed of the NFC overall. Once again, the Bears squeaked out a win in a game that things didn't totally go their way. Head coach Ben Johnson deserves a lot of credit for the way he's coached this football team. They respond to the schemes that he comes up with on offense; they never quit on the game, no matter how bleak things look, and winning follows him. Under center, Williams completed 19-of-34 passes for 250 yards and two touchdown passes. He did a great job of spreading the ball all over the field, down his top receivers in Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III, throughout the fourth quarter and overtime, including the big winner to Moore. In the rushing game, Kyle Monangai and D'Andre Swift combined to get over 100 yards. They were not responsible for any of the touchdowns, but they played a role in the team moving the ball down the field when the game was on the line. Injuries played a role in this game. The Packers were without Micah Parsons, who may be the best non-QB in the NFL. That affected their pass rush a lot, but they still managed to have a good defensive game without him. Packers running back Josh Jacobs was active, but his role decreased as the game went on. He is still dealing with his injury issues. The big story in this regard is quarterback Jordan Love. He was knocked out of the game with a concussion on a hit from defensive end Austin Booker. Backup Malik Willis came into the game and played as well as anyone would have expected, but the Bears found a way to beat him in the end. Now the Bears have wins over the Packers and Philadelphia Eagles in the last handful of weeks. They have another big test with the San Francisco 49ers coming up in prime time next week. It's been a while since they have had 11 wins in a season, but there is still more work to do. Sciatica Is Not from a Slipped Disc. text_body: Story by Vincent Parise, Bears Wire Mon, Dec 29, 2025 · 3 min read 1 Add Yahoo Sports on Google Before the Chicago Bears could even take the field against the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday night, they were declared the NFC North champions after the Green Bay Packers lost on Saturday night. Despite a tough 42-38 loss in prime-time, the Bears have locked down a home playoff game. The Bears came into the weekend with a chance at being any of the top three seeds in the NFC. For this to be the first season under rookie head coach Ben Johnson, they’ve exceeded all expectations. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The 49ers are one of the teams competing for that top spot in the conference. It was a disastrous start for them and a perfect start for Chicago, however, as the first offensive play of the game was an interception returned for a touchdown by linebacker T.J. Edwards. Dec 28, 2025; Santa Clara, California, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) passes against the San Francisco 49ers in the first half at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images From there, the teams exchanged touchdowns throughout. It is the first regular-season game in NFL history to be tied at 7, 14, 21, 28, and 35. Tied up at 35, the Bears' defense got a stop for the first time in a while. The next offensive drive ended with just a field goal for the Bears, which was then answered by a 49ers touchdown to go up by four. With 2:05 remaining in regulation time, quarterback Caleb Williams had another opportunity to create a game-winning drive for the Bears. Succeeding would've given Chicago a league-leading seven wins when trailing within the final two minutes of the fourth quarter. Although they had a chance, they ran out of time as they couldn't find the endzone on fourth-and-4 on the final play of the game. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement For a young team, a rookie head coach, a second-year quarterback, and a roster loaded with injuries and illness, it was a valiant effort. They were not even supposed to be a playoff team this year, and they competed for the No. 1 seed in Week 17. They will be fine settling for the second or third seed as NFC North champions. Although the Bears' defense had a disastrous outing, this was a shootout from the beginning. The offense, which has tended to wait until the second half to play well, was incredible from the start. SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 28: Luther Burden III #10 of the Chicago Bears catches a pass for a touchdown against the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter of the game at Levi's Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Williams completed 25-of-42 passes for 330 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions or sacks. His top receiving target was receiver Luther Burden III, who had eight receptions for 138 yards and a score. Tight end Colston Loveland also deserves mention, as he had 94 yards on six receptions with a touchdown. The two rookies played incredibly and gave their quarterback a good target all game long. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The running game was solid. It wasn't as dominant as it normally is, but that is in part due to Williams picking apart the San Francisco defense. D'Andre Swift had nine carries for 54 yards, and two of those carries ended in the endzone. Rookie Kyle Monangai had 38 yards on eight carries. In this game, Ben Johnson went against Kyle Shanahan. The latter has been one of the best offensive coaches in the NFL for a long time now, and Johnson is catching up quickly. They both deserve mentions in the "Coach of the Year" discussion, and they clearly have evenly matched teams coming out of this game. Next up for the Bears is their regular season finale against the Detroit Lions , who blew Chicago out in Week 2. Now, Detroit will pay a visit to Soldier Field. The Lions are eliminated from playoff contention, but they would love to make sure that the Bears end the season on a low note. Expect Chicago to prepare well ahead of a very important playoff dress rehearsal. This article originally appeared on Bears Wire: Bears vs. 49ers: Instant analysis from Chicago’s Week 17 loss

text_body: BEARS Instant analysis from Bears' improbable comeback win vs. Packers Vincent Parise Bears Wire Dec. 20, 2025 Updated Dec. 21, 2025, 12:28 a.m. CT The Chicago Bears defeated the Green Bay Packers 22-16 in an overtime victory on Saturday night. Quarterback Caleb Williams threw a walk-off touchdown pass to receiver DJ Moore in overtime to secure the win. The Bears' offense struggled early, scoring zero points in the first half before mounting a fourth-quarter comeback. Green Bay's starting quarterback, Jordan Love, left the game with a concussion and was replaced by backup Malik Willis. With the win, the Bears remain in first place in the NFC North and hold the second seed in the NFC. The Chicago Bears defeated the Green Bay Packers, 22-16, in overtime on Saturday night. They were losing for most of the game, but they once again mounted some late-game heroics to find a way to pull out the improbable win. They recovered an onside kick, scored when it mattered most, and made the necessary plays in OT to get it done. The Bears did not have a perfect game. They are dealing with some injuries, but they found a way to win a football game that was incredibly difficult against their arch-rival. The offense was stag in the first half. They scored zero points in the first 30 minutes and were trailing 6-0 at halftime. The defense was playing its brand of "bend-don't-break," and it was enough. But the offense wasn't living up to its end of the bargain. In the second half, things didn't get off to a strong start during a miserable third quarter that totaled just three points for Chicago. But the fourth quarter was once again the turning point as the Bears rattled off three straight scoring drives, including two field goals and the game-tying touchdown from quarterback Caleb Williams to rookie receiver Jahdae Walker to force overtime. In overtime, once the Packers turned the ball over on downs, the Bears just needed one big play. After some short yard gains, Williams made a big throw to receiver DJ Moore down the field, which ended in the walk-off score. The Bears were in danger of being swept by the Packers. That would have put their playoff hopes in jeopardy, but they found a way to get it done. Losing would have proved that they are not worthy of being a playoff team with the elites in the NFC. Instead, they remain in first of the NFC North, which is a great division, and they will stick in the second seed of the NFC overall. Once again, the Bears squeaked out a win in a game that things didn't totally go their way. Head coach Ben Johnson deserves a lot of credit for the way he's coached this football team. They respond to the schemes that he comes up with on offense; they never quit on the game, no matter how bleak things look, and winning follows him. Under center, Williams completed 19-of-34 passes for 250 yards and two touchdown passes. He did a great job of spreading the ball all over the field, down his top receivers in Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III, throughout the fourth quarter and overtime, including the big winner to Moore. In the rushing game, Kyle Monangai and D'Andre Swift combined to get over 100 yards. They were not responsible for any of the touchdowns, but they played a role in the team moving the ball down the field when the game was on the line. Injuries played a role in this game. The Packers were without Micah Parsons, who may be the best non-QB in the NFL. That affected their pass rush a lot, but they still managed to have a good defensive game without him. Packers running back Josh Jacobs was active, but his role decreased as the game went on. He is still dealing with his injury issues. The big story in this regard is quarterback Jordan Love. He was knocked out of the game with a concussion on a hit from defensive end Austin Booker. Backup Malik Willis came into the game and played as well as anyone would have expected, but the Bears found a way to beat him in the end. Brock Huard: ‘We haven’t seen many defenses like’ these Seahawks With their win Sunday night over the Chicago Bears, the 49ers improved to 12-4 heading into next week’s regular season finale against the 13-3 Seahawks. That means San Francisco kept alive its hopes of winning the NFC West and NFC’s No. 1 seed to the postseason, which it would clinch with a win over Seattle. But the Seahawks, who will be the only 13-win team in the NFC entering the final week of play, can do the same by beating the Niners. Next week’s Seahawks-49ers game has been announced for a 5 p.m. Saturday kickoff. The TV broadcast will air on ABC, while the Seattle Sports radio broadcast will begin at 2 p.m. with the pregame show. More: Time and TV set for Seahawks’ huge showdown vs. 49ers While the Seahawks and 49ers would have even 13-4 records if San Francisco wins next Saturday, that would clinch a tiebreaker for the 49ers, who already own the head-to-head advantage over Seattle thanks to their 17-13 win over the Hawks back in Week 1. San Francisco’s 42-38 win over Chicago on Sunday night took the NFC North-leading Bears (11-5) out of contention for the NFC’s top seed and the bye that comes with it in the playoffs. NFL standings There’s one other team that can tie for the best record in the division and conference: the Los Angeles Rams (11-4). But the Rams, who still have games against the Falcons (6-9) on Monday night and Arizona Cardinals (3-13) next week, cannot win a tiebreaker over either Seattle or San Francisco. If San Francisco beats Seattle and all three teams finish with identical 13-4 records, the Niners would win the division and No. 1 seed over the Rams and Seahawks based on the second tiebreaker, which is in-division record. San Francisco would improve to 5-1 in NFC West games with a win over the Seahawks while Seattle would drop to 3-3, and the Rams could be no better than 4-2. NFL tiebreaking procedures If the Seahawks beat the 49ers next week, it not only would clinch it all for them but also give them 14 wins in a season for the first time in team history.
